items.title: Estelle Perrault at 38Riv and Rémi Toulon Trio at Le Melville
items.summary: Two same-day Paris jazz options: Estelle Perrault's Motherly Voices cycle in the 4th arrondissement and a longer Rémi Toulon piano-trio set in the 8th.

items.title: FogDrive controlled adverse-weather perception and MegaSlide-DiT host-owned model state
items.summary: FogDrive provides matched clean and graded-fog multimodal scenes for sensor-fusion evaluation; MegaSlide-DiT adapts a pretrained 105B video DiT by keeping persistent state in host RAM and streaming transient GPU shards.

items.title: Wavelet trees
items.summary: Recursive alphabet partitioning plus rank/select bitvectors supports access, rank, select and range-quantile queries in succinct or compressed sequence representations.

items.title: Traction-force-activated endogenous growth-factor delivery
items.summary: Scaffold-anchored inhibitory aptamers harvest growth factors and release them when adhering or migrating cells mechanically unfold the construct, coupling delivery to local repair activity.

items.title: Different Washington bargaining systems and French compute value capture
items.summary: Zelenskiy and Netanyahu seek different forms of US leverage under distinct material and diplomatic constraints; France's data-centre buildout may localize grid and land costs while importing much of the high-value stack.

items.title: Installed data-centre megawatts are not a sovereignty metric
items.summary: Strategic compute capacity depends on ownership, access rights, domestic value capture, grid opportunity cost and productive use rather than aggregate capex or server-hall capacity alone.

items.title: Marx on relative social requirements
items.summary: The house comparison in Wage Labour and Capital shows how material adequacy is socially relational: an unchanged good can become inadequate as production, surrounding consumption and customary participation standards change.

items.title: Ferguson on undesigned institutions; Douglass on demands and concessions
items.summary: Ferguson warns that institutions can emerge without a designer and need not therefore be legitimate; Douglass ties reform to organized pressure rather than rulers' voluntary moral development.

items.title: à la rigueur
items.summary: An everyday phrase meaning at a pinch or if absolutely necessary, usually marking a reluctant but acceptable fallback and differing from a worst-case au pire scenario.

items.title: Aymara can map the known past in front and the unknown future behind
items.summary: Aymara temporal vocabulary and gesture provide evidence for a visibility-based spatial mapping in which the seen past is in front and the unknowable future behind.

items.title: Preface paradox
items.summary: An author rationally believes every individually well-supported claim in a long book while also rationally believing that at least one claim is false, creating tension between fallibility, conjunction and consistency.
